text: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.
I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you greatly."
Abram fell facedown, and God spoke with him, saying:

versions.text: Abram fell facedown, and God said to him:
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses דִּבֵּר אִתּוֹ ("spoke with him") plus לֵאמֹר, indicating conversational address; "spoke with him, saying" better reflects the wording and sets up the direct speech that follows.

text: "As for me, this is my covenant with you: you will be the father of a multitude of nations.
No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will come from you.
I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, an everlasting covenant: I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
And I will give to you and to your descendants after you the land where you now live as a stranger—all the land of Canaan—as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God."
Then God said to Abraham, "As for you, you are to keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.
This is my covenant, which you are to keep, between me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.
You shall have the flesh of your foreskin circumcised, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

versions.text: You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לְאוֹת בְּרִית is indefinite ("a sign of the covenant"); the definite article overstates the wording. Also note the Hebrew has plural "your foreskins" addressed to the community, which the singular here collapses but reads acceptably.

versions.text: You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וּנְמַלְתֶּם is a niphal (passive/reflexive) form: the addressees are the ones circumcised, not the ones performing the act on someone else. The active "You shall circumcise" makes the hearers the agents, which shifts the sense. A passive rendering keeps the accusative "the flesh of your foreskin" while restoring the voice, and it matches the passive phrasing used later in verses 12-14.

text: Every male among you, throughout your generations, shall be circumcised when he is eight days old—whether born in your household or bought with silver from a foreigner, one who is not of your own offspring.
Both the one born in your household and the one bought with your silver must be circumcised, so that my covenant may be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
Any uncircumcised male who has not had the flesh of his foreskin circumcised shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.

versions.text: Any uncircumcised male, who has not had the flesh of his foreskin circumcised, shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant."
versions.explanation: The commas make the relative clause non-restrictive, which changes the sense. The Hebrew clause is restrictive (defining which male), so the commas should be removed; this also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: God also said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you shall no longer call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah.
I will bless her, and I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will become nations; kings of peoples will come from her."
Then Abraham fell facedown and laughed, saying to himself, "Can a child be born to a man a hundred years old? Can Sarah bear a child at ninety?"
And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live in your presence!"

versions.text: And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live under your blessing!"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לְפָנֶיךָ literally means "before you / in your presence." "Under your blessing" is an interpretive expansion that introduces a concept (blessing) not in the Hebrew here; a more literal rendering preserves the idiom and still reads naturally.

text: But God said, "No—Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will father twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation.
But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year."
When he had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.

That very day Abraham took Ishmael his son, everyone born in his household, and everyone bought with his silver—every male among the men of Abraham's household—and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins, just as God had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised,
and his son Ishmael was thirteen when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on that very day,
and all the men of his household—those born in his house and those bought with silver from a foreigner—were circumcised with him.
